args.title: checkout-api: rolled back v2.3.1 → v2.3.0 due to failing health checks in all regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to production. At detection, all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1 with healthy=false and an error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously marked healthy in production (v2.2.9 was the prior healthy release; v2.3.1-rc was a staging-only release and was also unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate). The rollback reported status "rolled_out" and current version across us-east, us-west, and eu-west is now v2.3.0.

Note: this was a rollback to an already-proven-healthy version, so no change-manager approval was required. Next steps: confirm health/error rate recovery across all regions, then investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures before any re-deploy attempt.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Diagnosis**
- checkout-api was on **v2.3.1** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with `healthy: false` and an error rate of ~18%.
- Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), then v2.3.1 (unhealthy). There was also a `v2.3.1-rc` entry, but that was a **staging** release and was itself unhealthy — not a valid rollback target and not the cause of a production-only decision.
- Selected target: **v2.3.0**, the most recent release healthy in production.

**Action taken**
- Rolled back checkout-api to **v2.3.0** across all production regions. Result: `rolled_out`.
- Verified post-rollback: all three regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to ~0.2% (from 18%).

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on-call paged. (The first create_incident call timed out; I confirmed via `list_incidents` that no incident had actually been created, then retried successfully with the same idempotency key — so there's exactly one incident, not a duplicate.)

**Notes worth flagging**
- No change-manager approval was needed here: that policy applies to deploying a version that has never been healthy in production, whereas v2.3.0 was an already-proven-healthy version being rolled back to.
- The root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet known. I'd recommend treating that investigation as the follow-up — v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed until it's understood and fixed.
